column1: Stir the water, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl until the yeast dissolves. Add the flour and stir with a wooden spoon until smooth.
Cover with a damp towel and let rise 30 minutes.
Oil your hands and fold the dough over itself twice in the bowl. Cover and let rise another 30 minutes.
Fold once more, cover, and refrigerate at least 12 hours. Letting it ferment overnight is better: the slow cold rise gives more flavor and a lighter, airier crumb.
Oil 4 Le Creuset Mini Round Cocotte pots. Gently divide the cold dough into 4 equal pieces, place one in each pot for one serving per pot, and let rise 2–3 hours until puffy.
Drizzle with olive oil, oil your fingers, and poke dimples all over. Top with honey, rosemary and salt.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for about 25 minutes until golden brown.
